name: matlab-command-window
description: A better Command Window for the official MATLAB extension: HTML output with clickable error links, collapsible output, completion pop-up, help tooltips and Stop, attached to the MATLAB the official extension already runs (no second MATLAB). Not affiliated with or endorsed by MathWorks.

matlabCommandWindow.autoConnect.markdownDescription: Connect to the shared MATLAB when the Command Window is shown, and reconnect when `shareMATLABSession()` is run again.

matlabCommandWindow.languageServerPath.markdownDescription: The MATLAB language server used to connect (`.../server/out/index.js`). Leave empty to use the one inside the installed official MATLAB extension (`MathWorks.language-matlab`).

matlabCommandWindow.collapseLongOutput.markdownDescription: Collapse the output of a command to a few lines once it finishes when it is longer than 40 lines, with a button to show it all.

matlabCommandWindow.workspaceBesideComma.markdownDescription: Put the MATLAB extension's **Workspace** view beside the Command Window in the panel, the first time the Command Window opens. Afterwards you can move it anywhere; VS Code remembers. Turn off to move it back to the MATLAB side bar.

matlabCommandWindow.historyPopup.markdownDescription: **Up** opens the Command History pop-up, as in MATLAB: arrows move, **Enter** runs, **Right** puts the command on the line, **Shift+Up/Down** selects several. Turn off to recall commands on the input line instead.

matlabCommandWindow.editorHover.markdownDescription: Hover a name in a `.m` file to see its usage and description from the connected MATLAB's own `help` (and a link to its file and MathWorks documentation). Only while the Command Window is connected and MATLAB is idle or at K>>.

matlabCommandWindow.runInCommandWindow.markdownDescription: Run MATLAB files in this Command Window: **F5** runs the file, **Ctrl+Enter** the current `%%` section, **Shift+Enter** the selection, instead of the MATLAB extension's terminal. The editor keeps the focus. Ctrl+Enter and Shift+Enter also work at K>> (F5 stays the debugger's Continue). When MATLAB stops at a breakpoint, the Command Window (K>>) stays in front instead of the MATLAB terminal. Turn off to give these keys back to the MATLAB extension.
